newsitem.title: GERMANY: SAA adds Zurich/Paris, Amsterdam, Denmark flights.
newsitem.headline: SAA adds Zurich/Paris, Amsterdam, Denmark flights.

text.p: South African Airways will extend its European hub strategy from July with new flights and more code-share services, a senior manager said.
SAA will double its Boeing 747-400 flights to Zurich, extending to Paris, to four from two a week from July 1, Hans-Peter Fraembs, SAA central Europe manager, said.
Additionally, three of the carrier's daily South Africa-Frankfurt services would be extended to Amsterdam and another two flights would continue to Copenhagen, he told Reuters in an interview.
But it was still unclear whether an eighth Frankfurt flight would launch from July 1 or be delayed until the winter schedule.
The airline would also extend its code-share partnership with Deutsche Lufthansa AG with joint numbers on domestic flights from July, Fraembs said.
At a later stage, SAA and Lufthansa would code-share on routes in central Europe and southern Africa but this remained a planning option at present, he added.
Fraembs said: "The SAA Europe strategy is to concentrate on three hubs -- London, Frankfurt and Zurich.
"In central Europe, Lufthansa acts as a feeder for SAA into Frankfurt and British Midland is a feeder in London," he added.
The four weekly flights to Zurich and on to Paris would allow SAA to target the steadily growing Swiss market, France and southern European countries, he said.

SAA now had partnerships with several airlines in the emerging Lufthansa-based global alliance but had a long-standing and successful code-share agreement with American Airlines for transatlantic services, Fraembs noted.

"It is positive that we are in a strong alliance with Lufthansa although we have different U.S. partners. Lufthansa respects our American Airlines relationship and SAA respects their United links," he said.
Fraembs added: "SAA is a niche carrier, not a global carrier. We have the responsibility within this group to cover flights to South Africa and southern Africa."
